originalTitle: Snowfall in Times Square, NYC | Walking in New York City in the Winter Snow, 4k
sourceDescription: Snowfall walk in Times Square, New York City. It's been a year since I last visited New York. I didn't plan a route for this video. My friend living in Brooklyn sent me a text that there would be snowfall in New York the following morning, so I made a 14-hour drive up to New York the day before and crashed in my hotel room in Times Square at 2 am. The next morning it started to snow, but I was still totally exhausted from the night before. This walk is a bit aimless and mostly around Times Square because I had to start work immediately after and was already out of it. I wanted to capture the contrast between this video and my previous videos from 2019. New York is so quiet. Early apologies for all of the cuts in the recording. I stopped to clear water residue off of my camera lens every so often. Binaural audio for an immersive experience. Information: Experience the timeless beauty of Rome in this extensive walking tour, taking you through the Eternal City's most iconic landmarks. From the historic Spanish Steps to the grand Colosseum, this tour covers nearly four hours of Rome’s architectural wonders, charming piazzas, and ancient ruins. Whether you're revisiting your favorite Roman spots or discovering them for the first time, this walking tour offers an in-depth journey through one of the most remarkable cities in the world. History: Rome’s history spans over 2,500 years, and this tour offers a glimpse into some of its most significant monuments. Starting at the Spanish Steps (1:25), which were built in the early 18th century and remain one of Rome’s most popular meeting spots, you’ll pass through the Trevi Fountain (32:11), an 18th-century Baroque masterpiece where visitors toss coins to ensure their return to Rome. At the Pantheon (55:18), you'll explore the best-preserved Roman temple, dating back to 125 AD, and learn about its transformation into a Christian church. The tour also takes you to the Altar of the Fatherland (2:35:20), a monumental tribute to Italy's first king, Victor Emmanuel II, and finishes with a close-up view of the Colosseum (3:37:38), the largest amphitheater ever built, which once hosted gladiatorial battles. Tourist Tips: Begin your tour at the Spanish Steps (1:25) to enjoy the early morning light before the crowds gather. Toss a coin into the Trevi Fountain (32:11) to ensure a future trip to Rome—just be sure to do it with your right hand over your left shoulder! Take a moment to admire the artistry at the Church of St. Louis of the French (1:11:00), which houses famous paintings by Caravaggio. Enjoy the vibrant atmosphere of Piazza Navona (1:19:51), surrounded by Baroque architecture and street performers. Climb up Capitoline Hill (2:10:43) for incredible views of the Roman Forum and cityscape. End your tour at the Colosseum (3:37:38), where you can imagine the grand gladiatorial contests that once took place within its walls. #ProwalkTours #Walkingtour #Rome

sourceDescription: This walking video was recorded in 4k in Berlin, the capital of Germany 🇩🇪 Berlin is the capital and a state of the Federal Republic of Germany. With about 3.7 million inhabitants, the city is the most populous and, with 892 square kilometers, the largest municipality in Germany, as well as the most populous city in the European Union. The city has the third highest population density in Germany with 4108 inhabitants per square kilometer. Nearly 4.7 million inhabitants live in the Berlin agglomeration, and about 6.2 million in the Berlin-Brandenburg capital region. Berlin is considered a world city of culture, politics, media and science. The local universities and research institutions, local sports and museums enjoy an international reputation. The metropolis holds the UNESCO title of City of Design and is one of the continent's most visited centers. Its architecture, festivities and nightlife are world-renowned. After the end of World War II, the city was subject to a four-power status in 1945; East Berlin functioned as the capital of the socialist German Democratic Republic from 1949, while West Berlin was closely aligned with the liberal-democratic Federal Republic. With the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 and German reunification in 1990, the two halves of the city grew together again and Berlin regained its role as the all-German capital. sourceDescription: My dear friends, welcome to a truly magical journey. In this video, we invite you to join us for a peaceful, atmospheric walk through Hallstatt, often hailed as the most beautiful village in Europe. originalTitle: Amsterdam Red Light District Night Walk 🇳🇱 | De Wallen, Historic Streets & Nightlife Atmosphere (4K)
sourceDescription: Amsterdam night walking tour through De Wallen — the Red Light District — from Central Station along Zeedijk to the Oude Kerk, Amsterdam's oldest building. A 26-minute walk through the historic heart of Amsterdam, Netherlands. The Red Light District begins at 11:39. Filmed in 4K60fps with binaural audio. De Wallen (meaning "the walls") is Amsterdam's oldest neighborhood and the core of the city's medieval center. The walk begins at Centraal Station, follows Zeedijk — one of Amsterdam's earliest streets dating back to the 14th-century sea dike — through the illuminated canals and nightlife of the Red Light District, and ends at the Oude Kerk, founded around 1213 and consecrated in 1306 as Amsterdam's first parish church. Ideal for virtual travel, treadmill walks, and ambient atmosphere. Best with headphones. ⭐ Don't miss: The Red Light District (De Wallen) starts at 11:39, Oude Kerk at 16:59. 📅 Location: Amsterdam, North Holland, Netherlands 🗺️ Map of the Walk: https://www.google.com/maps/d/edit?mid=1WiBZScN1pPOgcJAXopbKyeLu-wRACzs&usp=sharing ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ⏱️ TOUR TIMELINE ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 0:00 Central Station ⭐ 4:46 Zeedijk Street ⭐ 11:39 Red Light District (De Wallen) ⭐ 16:59 Oude Kerk (Old Church) ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ⛪ ABOUT DE WALLEN & THE OUDE KERK ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ The Oude Kerk is Amsterdam's oldest surviving building. Founded around 1213 as a wooden chapel, it was consecrated in 1306 by the Bishop of Utrecht and dedicated to Saint Nicholas, the patron saint of sailors. Its wooden vault ceiling, built around 1390 from Estonian oak, is the largest medieval wooden vault in Europe. The floor is paved with roughly 2,500 gravestones beneath which approximately 60,000 Amsterdam citizens are buried, including Saskia van Uylenburgh — Rembrandt's wife — who was laid to rest here in 1642. The church became Calvinist after the Dutch Reformation of 1578 and remains an active parish today, sitting quietly at the center of De Wallen as both a place of worship and contemporary art venue. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 📽 MORE WALKING TOURS ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 🌇 Evening Walks: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLSOO4vYXpMCeOzhVqdArVIJ9aiS1Xhw6O 🎄 Christmas Markets: https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLSOO4vYXpMCd2nqHyPaDtgxkf_BsAuQCt&si=0YU1zhv0tLbwm8u6 🍕 Italy: https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLSOO4vYXpMCc6k7EuMhr764qCNeXDrxpj&si=aYfLAtNw1eGc560w 🌍 Complete List: http://www.prowalks.com/videos ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 📢 SUPPORT & CONNECT 📢 ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 🌍 Website: https://www.prowalktours.com 📧 Email: info@prowalktours.com 🔔 Subscribe for more! originalTitle: Spring Rainy Day in SWITZERLAND 🌧️ Most Beautiful Villages 🇨🇭 Brienz Walking in the Rain 4K
sourceDescription: 🎬 Spring Rainy Day in SWITZERLAND 🌧️ Most Beautiful Villages 🇨🇭 Brienz Walking in the Rain 4K Welcome to one of the most picturesque corners of Switzerland — the lakeside village of Brienz, nestled on the northern shore of Lake Brienz and surrounded by dramatic alpine scenery. Today, we’ll take a peaceful walk through the rain-soaked streets, breathe in the fresh spring air, and discover what makes this quiet place so unique. 🏘️ What Makes Brienz Special? Woodcarving Capital of Switzerland Brienz is famous for its woodcarving tradition. It’s home to the School of Woodcarving — the only one of its kind in Switzerland. The buildings themselves are decorated with hand-carved designs, giving the village the look of a fairytale scene. Oberdorf – The Old Village The historic heart of Brienz, known as Oberdorf, features narrow alleys, stone pathways, and centuries-old chalets — each with its own character. It’s a perfect place for a quiet walk, especially on a rainy day when the streets are almost empty. Brienzer Rothorn Railway Brienz is also the starting point of the Brienzer Rothorn Bahn, a historic cogwheel railway that climbs to one of the region’s highest peaks. While the train may not run in early spring, you can still enjoy stunning views of the snow-covered mountains from the lakeside promenade. Ballenberg Open-Air Museum Just a short drive from Brienz, the Ballenberg Museum offers a journey through time — with over 100 traditional Swiss buildings from all across the country, brought together in one beautiful outdoor setting. 🌿 Spring in Brienz Spring arrives slowly here. The first wildflowers begin to bloom, and the air smells of damp earth and fresh-cut wood. Birds sing from the treetops, mountain streams bubble in the distance, and the soft sound of cowbells echoes through the valleys — a soundtrack perfectly suited to this peaceful alpine village. 🧭 Getting There Brienz is located between Interlaken and Lucerne. It’s easily reached by train — just 25 minutes from Interlaken — along one of the most scenic rail routes in the country. Arrive in the morning and take your time soaking in the atmosphere of this magical lakeside escape. Rain in Brienz isn't gloomy — it's poetic. It reveals the quiet charm of the village in new ways: in reflections on the pavement, in the scent of rain on old wood, in the mist rising from the lake. This is a place for slow moments, deep breaths, and quiet wonder.

The Moscow International Business Center (MIBC), also known as Moscow-City, is an under construction commercial development in Moscow, the capital of Russia. The project occupies an area of 60 hectares, and is located just east of the Third Ring Road at the western edge of the Presnensky District in the Central Administrative Okrug. Construction of the MIBC takes place on the Presnenskaya Embankment of the Moskva River, approximately 4 kilometers (2.5 mi) west of Red Square. The complex is a major financial centre in Europe, and is home to the highest numbers of skyscrapers in the continent. The Government of Moscow first conceived the project in 1992, as a mixed development of office, residential, retail and entertainment facilities. An estimated 250,000 – 300,000 people will be working in, living in, or visiting the complex at any given time. Vladivostok was founded on July 2, 1860, as a Russian military outpost on the shores of the Golden Horn Bay, and its name is often translated as Rule the East or Lord of the East, depending on the exact interpretation used. The settlement gained official town status in 1880, and by 1888 it had become the administrative center of the surrounding Primorskaya Oblast region, which spurred rapid local infrastructure development across the whole city. Completion of the Trans-Siberian Railway in 1903 made Vladivostok its eastern terminus, transforming the once-remote outpost into a major trade link connecting Europe and Asia together by rail for the very first time in history. The population grew from about 29,000 residents in 1897 to over 100,000 by 1914, and it now stands at roughly 600,000 people living in the city today, with the vast, large majority of them being ethnic Russian residents. Due to its strategic naval base, the Soviet government declared Vladivostok a closed city in 1958, barring most outside visitors and even many ordinary Soviet citizens until it finally reopened again in early January 1992. originalTitle: Walking tour - Tverskaya Street - Moscow 4k, Russia - HDR
sourceDescription: #Walkingtour #Moscow #walk Tverskaya Street known between 1935 and 1990 as Gorky Street is the main radial street in Moscow. The street runs Northwest from the central Manege Square in the direction of Saint Petersburg and terminates at the Garden Ring, giving the name to Tverskoy District. The route continues further as First Tverskaya-Yamskaya Street, Leningradsky Avenue and Leningradskoye Highway. Tourists are told that Tverskaya Street existed as early as the 12th century. Its importance for the medieval city was immense, as it connected Moscow with its superior, and later chief rival, Tver. At that time, the thoroughfare crossed the Neglinnaya River. In the 17th and 18th centuries, Tverskaya Street was renowned as the centre of Moscow's social life. The nobility considered it fashionable to settle in this district. The mayor's residence among a number of other historic buildings was moved about 14 meters for the widening of the Gorky Street during Stalin's time. On the square before it stands a statue of the legendary founder of Moscow, Yuri Dolgoruky, erected for the city's 800th anniversary. During the imperial period, the importance of the thoroughfare was highlighted by the fact that it was through this street that the tsars arrived from the Northern capital to stay at their Kremlin residence. Several triumphal arches were constructed to commemorate coronation ceremonies. In 1792, the Tverskaya Square was laid out before the residence of the governor of Moscow as a staging ground for mass processions and parades. In 1947, the square was decorated with an equestrian statue of Prince Yury Dolgoruky, founder of Moscow. Towards the end of the 19th century, the street was reconstructed, with stately neoclassical mansions giving way to grandiose commercial buildings in an eclectic mixture of historical styles. A characteristic edifice of the time is the eclectic Hotel National, Moscow (1901-1903), whose interior is a landmark of Russian Art Nouveau. In 1888 the actor, theatre director and founder of the Moscow Art Theatre, Constantin Stanislavski, rented the Ginzburg House on the street and had it converted into a luxurious clubhouse with its own large stage and several exhibition rooms, in order to house his newly formed Society of Art and Literature. The street was renamed in 1932 for Maxim Gorky, the Russian writer and revolutionary admired by both Vladimir Lenin and Josef Stalin. Further expansion occurred in line with Joseph Stalin's 1935 master plan. During that period, all the churches and most other historic buildings were torn down in order to widen the street and replace low-rise buildings with larger, early Stalinist apartment blocks and government offices. When Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev assumed power, he encouraged a return to the country's old Russian names. Thus, the street's name became "Tverskaya Street" again, after a 55-year interlude as Gorky Street. Tverskaya Street is the most expensive shopping street in Moscow and Russia. According to an index published by global real estate company Colliers International in 2008, it is now the third most expensive street in the world, based on commercial rental fees. It is the center of the city's nightlife and entertainment. ========================= Welcome to AboutWalk Channel! We walk along the famous streets in the big cities of the World. sourceDescription: #Stalingrad #Walkingtour #Мамаевкурган Mamayev Kurgan is a dominant height overlooking the city of Volgograd (formerly Stalingrad) in Southern Russia. The name in Russian means "tumulus of Mamai". The formation is dominated by a memorial complex commemorating the Battle of Stalingrad (August 1942 to February 1943). The battle, a hard-fought Soviet victory over Axis forces on the Eastern Front of World War II, turned into one of the bloodiest battles in human history. At the time of its installation in 1967 the statue, named The Motherland Calls, formed the largest free-standing sculpture in the world; today it is the tallest sculpture of a woman in the world. When forces of the German Sixth Army launched their attack against the city centre of Stalingrad on 13 September 1942, Mamayev Kurgan (appearing in military maps as "Height 102.0") saw particularly fierce fighting between the German attackers and the defending soldiers of the Soviet 62nd Army. Control of the hill became vitally important, as it offered control over the city. The hill changed hands several times. By 27 September, the Germans again captured half of Mamayev Kurgan. The Soviets held their own positions on the slopes of the hill, as the 284th Rifle Division defended the key stronghold. The defenders held out until 26 January 1943, when the counterattacking Soviet forces relieved them. The battle of the city ended one week later with an utter German defeat. After the war, the Soviet authorities commissioned the enormous Mamayev Kurgan memorial complex. Vasily Chuikov, who led Soviet forces at Stalingrad, lies buried at Mamayev Kurgan, the only Marshal of the Soviet Union to be buried outside Moscow. The monumental memorial was constructed between 1959 and 1967, and is crowned by a huge allegorical statue of the Motherland on the top of the hill. The monument, designed by Yevgeny Vuchetich, has the full name The Motherland Calls! It consists of a concrete sculpture, 52 metres tall, and 85 metres from the feet to the tip of the 27-metre sword, dominating the skyline of the city of Stalingrad (later renamed Volgograd). The construction uses concrete, except for the stainless-steel blade of the sword, and is held on its plinth solely by its own weight. The statue is evocative of classical Greek representations of Nike, in particular the flowing drapery, similar to that of the Nike of Samothrace. ========================= Welcome to AboutWalk Channel! The street runs Northwest from the central Manege Square in the direction of Saint Petersburg and terminates at the Garden Ring, giving the name to Tverskoy District. The route continues further as First Tverskaya-Yamskaya Street, Leningradsky Avenue and Leningradskoye Highway. Middle Ages to 18th century Tourists are told that Tverskaya Street existed as early as the 12th century. Its importance for the medieval city was immense, as it connected Moscow with its superior, and later chief rival, Tver. At that time, the thoroughfare crossed the Neglinnaya River. The first stone bridge across the Neglinnaya was set up in 1595. In the 17th and 18th centuries, Tverskaya Street was renowned as the centre of Moscow's social life. The nobility considered it fashionable to settle in this district. Among the Palladian mansions dating from the reign of Catherine the Great are the residence of the mayor of Moscow (1778–82, rebuilt in ), and the English Club (1780s). The mayor's residence among a number of other historic buildings was moved about 14 meters for the widening of the Gorky Street during Stalin's time. On the square before it stands a statue of the legendary founder of Moscow, Yuri Dolgoruky, erected for the city's 800th anniversary. During the imperial period, the importance of the thoroughfare was highlighted by the fact that it was through this street that the tsars arrived from the Northern capital to stay at their Kremlin residence. Several triumphal arches were constructed to commemorate coronation ceremonies. In 1792, the Tverskaya Square was laid out before the residence of the governor of Moscow as a staging ground for mass processions and parades. sourceDescription: Nevsky Prospect (Russian: Не́вский проспе́кт, tr. Nevsky Prospekt, IPA: [ˈnʲɛfskʲɪj prɐˈspʲɛkt]) is the main street (high street) in the federal city of St. Petersburg in Russia. It takes its name from the Alexander Nevsky Lavra, the monastery which stands at the eastern end of the street, and which in turn commemorates the Russian hero Prince Saint Alexander Nevsky (1221–1263). Following his founding of Saint Petersburg in 1703, Tsar Peter I planned the course of the street as the beginning of the road to Novgorod and Moscow. The avenue runs from the Admiralty in the west to the Moscow Railway Station and, after veering slightly southwards at Vosstaniya Square, to the Alexander Nevsky Lavra. originalTitle: [4K] 🇷🇺 Moscow Evening Walk. Nikolskaya Street. Kitay-gorod
sourceDescription: Moscow by sunset walking tour among Nikolskaya Street in Kitay-gorod. Nikolskaya Street (Russian: Никольская улица) is a pedestrian street in the Kitay-Gorod of Moscow. It connects Red Square and Lubyanka Square. It was known as the Street of the 25th of October between 1935 and 1990. The north side of the street is lined with historic buildings, such as the Kazan Cathedral, the Old Mint, Monastery of the Holy Saviour, Greek Monastery of St. Nicholas (from which this street takes its name), and the former Holy Synod Printing Offices, Russia's first publishing house. The south side contains the GUM and the Dormition Church, an example of the Naryshkin Baroque underwritten by the Saltykov boyar family in 1691. Before Stalin's reconstruction of downtown Moscow, the street led to the Vladimir Gates of the Kitay-Gorod wall (1534-38) which used to dominate the Lubyanka Square. Another Naryshkin Baroque church, dating from 1694, adjoined the gate, as did the more recent chapel of St. Pantaleon with a large cupola. All these buildings were razed in 1934. The Nikolskaya Street and the neighbouring Tretyakovsky Proyezd are the center of Moscow's traditional luxury shopping district. It was pedestrianized in August 2013. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolskaya_Street Filmed on iPhone 11. Handheld. sourceDescription: Kazan (/kəˈzæn, -ˈzɑːn/; Russian: Каза́нь, IPA: [kɐˈzanʲ]); Tatar: Казан IPA: [qɑzan], is the capital and largest city of the Republic of Tatarstan in Russia. The city lies at the confluence of the Volga and the Kazanka rivers, covering an area of 425.3 square kilometres (164.2 square miles), with a population of over 1.2 million residents, up to roughly 1.6 million residents in the urban agglomeration. Kazan is the fifth-largest city in Russia, and the most populous city on the Volga, as well as the Volga Federal District. Kazan was founded in the late 13th century by the Golden Horde. In 1438, Kazan became the capital of the Khanate of Kazan. In 1552, Kazan was captured by Ivan the Terrible and became a part of Russia. The city was seized and largely destroyed during Pugachev's Rebellion of 1773–1775, but was later rebuilt during the reign of Catherine the Great. In the following centuries, Kazan grew to become a major industrial, cultural and religious centre of Russia. In 1920, after the Russian SFSR became a part of the Soviet Union, Kazan became the capital of the Tatar ASSR. After the dissolution of the Soviet Union, Kazan stayed as the capital of the Republic of Tatarstan. Kazan is renowned for its vibrant mix of Tatar and Russian cultures. In 2015, 2.1 million tourists visited Kazan, and 1.5 million tourists visited the Kazan Kremlin, a World Heritage Site. In April 2009, the Russian Patent Office granted Kazan the right to brand itself as the "Third Capital of Russia". In 2009 it was chosen as the "Sports capital of Russia",and it still is referred to as such. Kazan hosted the 2013 Summer Universiade, and was one of the host cities of the 2018 FIFA World Cup. Baumana Street (Russian: улица Баумана; Tatar: Бауман урамы) is a pedestrian street in the heart of Kazan, the capital of Tatarstan, Russia. It is named after Nikolay Bauman, a Russian revolutionary, and is located in the central part of the city. The street starts at the foot of the Kremlin and reaches Tukay Square, the central square in the city. Baumana Street is paved with multicoloured bricks; some benches and two lines of lanterns are set there. There are also planted lindens on the street. originalTitle: 【4K】Snowfall in Saint-Petersburg (Christmas Walk) Night walk in Saint-Petersburg in the Winter Snow
sourceDescription: Christmas in Russia, commemorating the birth of Jesus Christ, is celebrated on 25 December in the Julian calendar used by the church, which falls on 7 January in the common Gregorian calendar. Christmas is considered a high holiday by the Russian Orthodox Church, one of the 12 Great Feasts, and one of only four of which are preceded by a period of fasting. History In Russia, the Christmas holiday became the official celebration with the baptism of Rus' ordered by Prince Vladimir in the late 10th century. However, given the early Christian community Kievan Rus', celebration may have a longer history. During the early-mid Soviet period, religious celebrations were discouraged by the official state policy of atheism until 1936, but despite this, Christmas was marked by the Soviet regime on 25 December. Christmas tree and related decorations, the visit by gift-giving "Ded Moroz" (Дед Мороз "Grandfather Frost") and his granddaughter, "Snegurochka" (Снегурочка "The Snowmaiden"). Religious services On Christmas Eve, 6 January, there are several long services, including the Royal Hours and Vespers combined with the Divine Liturgy. The family will then return home for the traditional Christmas Eve (Holy Supper), which consists of 12 dishes, one to honour each of the Twelve Apostles. Devout families will then return to church for the All Night Vigil. Then again, on Christmas Morning, they return to attend the Morning Divine Liturgy of the Nativity. Since 1992 Christmas has become a national holiday in Russia, as part of the ten-day holiday at the start of the new year. Traditional festive cuisine Principal dishes on the Christmas table in old Russia included a variety of pork (roasted pig), stuffed pig's head, roasted meat chunks, jelly (kholodets), and aspic. Christmas dinner also included many other meats: goose with apples, sour cream hare, venison, lamb, whole fish, etc.. The abundance of fried and baked meats, whole baked chicken, and fish on the festive table was associated with features of the Russian oven, which allowed successful preparation of large portions. Finely sliced meat and pork was cooked in pots with semi-traditional porridge. Pies were indispensable dishes for Christmas, as well as other holidays, and included both closed and open style pirogi (pirozhki, vatrushkas, coulibiacs, kurnik, saechki, shangi), kalachi, cooked casseroles, and blini. Fillings of every flavor were included (herbal, vegetable, fruit, mushrooms, meat, fish, cheese, mixed). Sweet dishes served on the Russian Christmas table included berries, fruit, candy, cakes, angel wings, biscuits, honey. Beverages included drinking broths (kompot and sweet soups, sbiten), kissel, and, from the beginning of the 18th century, Chinese tea. originalTitle: Volgograd (Stalingrad) Russia | Mamayev Kurgan - Walking tour - HDR 4k
sourceDescription: #Stalingrad #Walkingtour #Мамаевкурган Mamayev Kurgan is a dominant height overlooking the city of Volgograd (formerly Stalingrad) in Southern Russia. The name in Russian means "tumulus of Mamai". The formation is dominated by a memorial complex commemorating the Battle of Stalingrad (August 1942 to February 1943). The battle, a hard-fought Soviet victory over Axis forces on the Eastern Front of World War II, turned into one of the bloodiest battles in human history. At the time of its installation in 1967 the statue, named The Motherland Calls, formed the largest free-standing sculpture in the world; today it is the tallest sculpture of a woman in the world. When forces of the German Sixth Army launched their attack against the city centre of Stalingrad on 13 September 1942, Mamayev Kurgan (appearing in military maps as "Height 102.0") saw particularly fierce fighting between the German attackers and the defending soldiers of the Soviet 62nd Army. Control of the hill became vitally important, as it offered control over the city. The hill changed hands several times. By 27 September, the Germans again captured half of Mamayev Kurgan. The Soviets held their own positions on the slopes of the hill, as the 284th Rifle Division defended the key stronghold. The defenders held out until 26 January 1943, when the counterattacking Soviet forces relieved them. The battle of the city ended one week later with an utter German defeat. The monumental memorial was constructed between 1959 and 1967, and is crowned by a huge allegorical statue of the Motherland on the top of the hill. The monument, designed by Yevgeny Vuchetich, has the full name The Motherland Calls! It consists of a concrete sculpture, 52 metres tall, and 85 metres from the feet to the tip of the 27-metre sword, dominating the skyline of the city of Stalingrad (later renamed Volgograd). The construction uses concrete, except for the stainless-steel blade of the sword, and is held on its plinth solely by its own weight. The statue is evocative of classical Greek representations of Nike, in particular the flowing drapery, similar to that of the Nike of Samothrace. ========================= Welcome to AboutWalk Channel! We walk along the famous streets in the big cities of the World. You travel around the city. This may be the city of your dreams, in which you want to visit. originalTitle: 【4K】Walking in Kaliningrad (Königsberg), Russia
sourceDescription: Kaliningrad, formerly German (1255–1946) Königsberg, Polish Królewiec, city, seaport, and administrative centre of Kaliningrad oblast (region), Russia. Detached from the rest of the country, the city is an exclave of the Russian Federation. Kaliningrad lies on the Pregolya River just upstream from Frisches Lagoon. Formerly the capital of the dukes of Prussia and later the capital of East Prussia, the city was ceded to the Soviet Union in 1945 under the Potsdam agreement. The old town of Königsberg (“King’s Mountain”) grew up around the fortress built in 1255 by the Teutonic Knights on the advice of Přemysl Otakar II, king of Bohemia, after whom the place was named. Its first site was near the fishing town of Steindamm, but, after its destruction by the Prussians in 1263, it was rebuilt near where the city now stands. Königsberg received civic privileges in 1286 and entered the Hanseatic League in 1340. From 1457 it was the residence of the grand master of the Teutonic Knights, and from 1525 until 1618 the residence of the dukes of Prussia. The trade of Königsberg was much hindered by the constant shifting and silting up of the channels leading to its harbour, and the First Northern War (1655–60) did the city immense damage, but before the end of the 17th century it had almost recovered. In 1701, in the chapel of the castle, Elector Frederick III of Brandenburg crowned himself the first king of Prussia—as Frederick I. In 1724 Frederick William I of Prussia united nearby Löbenicht and Kneiphof with Königsberg to form a single city. Königsberg suffered severely during the Napoleonic Wars and was the scene of the deliberations that led to the successful uprising of Prussia against Napoleon. During the 19th century the opening of a railway system in East Prussia and Russia gave a new impetus to the city’s commerce, making it the principal outlet for such Russian staples as grain, seeds, flax, and hemp. Under Prussia and then Germany the town was, after Kiel, the main naval base on the Baltic Sea and a key to the defense of the eastern frontier. Its modern fortifications were begun in 1843 and completed in 1905. The city was besieged by the Russians unsuccessfully during World War I. In World War II, however, it was virtually destroyed by the Red Army after a two-month siege ending in April 1945. Left in ruins were the 14th-century cathedral, the grand castle begun by the Teutonic Knights, and the old university. Along with the extreme northern sector of East Prussia, Königsberg then passed to the sovereignty of the U.S.S.R. The new city—renamed Kaliningrad in 1946—was rebuilt and centred in what had been Königsberg’s northwestern suburbs and became a major industrial and commercial centre, connected by a 20-mile (32-kilometre) dredged channel to an outport and naval base along the Baltic called Baltiysk. The entire German population was evicted in 1947 and settled in West and East Germany. Hundreds of thousands of new settlers, primarily from Russia and Belarus, were recruited to live in the city, helping transform the urban landscape into a mosaic of old German buildings and landmarks—including the grave site of philosopher Immanuel Kant, a monument to dramatist and poet Friedrich Schiller, and several Gothic cathedrals—and Soviet developments, such as multistory apartment buildings constructed in the decades after World War II. The city was closed to foreigners until 1991. A significant share of the local population is involved in shuttle trade of clothing and footwear purchased in Poland. The city has fishing, engineering, lumber, machinery, and papermaking industries. To stimulate investment in Kaliningrad, a special economic zone that exempts from customs duties most imported and exported goods was established there. Transit traffic between the Kaliningrad exclave and the rest of Russia is conducted via Lithuania and Belarus. originalTitle: 【4K】Walking in Moscow, Tverskaya street to Red Square | Evening walk in Moscow, Russia
sourceDescription: In this walk we will visit one of the most famous streets in Moscow - Tverskaya street. The walk starts from Troilinsky lane to Manezhnaya square. The history of the street: Tverskaya street leads Northwest from the Kremlin. It starts from Manezhnaya square and ends at Triumfalnaya square. From 1932 to 1990, Tverskaya was called Gorky street and was much longer. Gorky street included the First Tverskaya-Yamskaya street, which runs from Triumfalnaya square to Tverskaya Zastava square. The name Maxim Gorky was given by Tverskaya in connection with the 40th anniversary of the writer's creative activity during his lifetime. There are two squares on Tverskaya street. This is Tverskaya square opposite the house of the Governor-General (later the Mossovet, the government of Moscow). It was created in 1792 and served for the daily divorce of the guard. Pushkin square is located at the intersection with the Boulevard ring, built on the site of the walls of the White city. Until 1937, it was called Strastnaya square. Tverskaya street was formed from the main road to Tver, the capital of the neighboring Principality and a rival of Moscow. Since the XV century, the Tver road has been connected with the road to Novgorod and its importance has grown. In 1504, the street was built up from the beginning only to the modern Pushkin square. Beyond it, the road to Tver ran through fields and groves. Already in the XVII century, Tverskaya was perceived as the main street of the city. Both foreign ambassadors and tsars entered Moscow in state on Tverskaya street. After the Foundation of St. Petersburg, Tverskaya became the road to the new capital. Since the reign of Peter the Great, it was customary to arrange triumphal arches on the squares along Tverskaya street on the occasion of holidays, military victories or coronations. Solemn processions along Tverskaya and other streets to the Kremlin played a big role in the life of the city. Thus, one of the processions under Peter I carried a real warship on ice rinks. The triumphal arches on Tverskaya street were temporary, wooden, and had to be dismantled after the festival. The memory of the triumphs of the past is preserved in the name of the triumphal square. The width of the main street of Moscow in the XVII century was only from 8.5 to 15 meters. In the XVIII century, the minimum width for large streets of the city was set at about 20 meters. Tverskaya remained this way until reconstruction in the 1930s. Due to the demolition of houses on the red lines, the width of Tverskaya was brought to 40 meters. During the reconstruction process, four large buildings were moved to new locations. These are Savvinsky farmstead of the architect I. S. Kuznetsov (1907, Tverskaya, 6 p. 6, in the courtyard), Mossovet (Tverskaya, 13), Eye hospital (Mamonovsky lane, 7) and house 21 in Bryusov lane. The fifth and so far the last house moved-Tverskaya, 18, the house of I. D. Sytin, stood in a new place in 1979. Along Tverskaya street, the rich and noble Muscovites preferred to build their own houses. The street consisted of large manors with services, among which were visible parish and house churches, as well as monasteries. Moiseyevsky monastery was located at the beginning of Tverskaya street, on the modern Manezhnaya square, abolished by decree in 1764 and soon demolished. The resurrection monastery existed from the XV century until the middle of the XVII century, when it was transformed into the courtyard of the Savvino-Storozhevsky monastery (Tverskaya street, 6). Strastnoy monastery stood on Pushkin square, was abolished in 1919, but the nuns lived in it until 1928. Destroyed in the late 1930s. In addition to the monasteries, it is worth noting two destroyed parish churches. Dmitry Solunsky Church - on the corner of Tverskaya and Tverskoy Boulevard and the Church of the Annunciation on the site of house 25/12, on the corner of Blagoveshchensk lane. The first intercity stagecoach that ran until 1851 passed through Tverskaya in 1820 to St Petersburg. In 1872, on the occasion of the opening of the Polytechnic exhibition, a horse – drawn railway was launched along the street-a horse-drawn tram, which was replaced in the early twentieth century by a tram. In 1933, the first trolleybus began to run along Tverskaya street. Today Tverskaya street is still the main street in Moscow. It is home to expensive hotels (national, Ritz Carlton, MARRIOTT Grand), well-known stores (yeliseyevsky, Moscow bookstore), cafes, restaurants, museums and theaters. The type of street is defined by houses in the style of Soviet classics of the mid-twentieth century. There is no such format on YouTube. Thank you for watching! Mamayev Kurgan is a dominant height overlooking the city of Volgograd (formerly Stalingrad) in Southern Russia. The name in Russian means "tumulus of Mamai". The formation is dominated by a memorial complex commemorating the Battle of Stalingrad (August 1942 to February 1943). The battle, a hard-fought Soviet victory over Axis forces on the Eastern Front of World War II, turned into one of the bloodiest battles in human history. At the time of its installation in 1967 the statue, named The Motherland Calls, formed the largest free-standing sculpture in the world; today it is the tallest sculpture of a woman in the world. The monumental memorial was constructed between 1959 and 1967, and is crowned by a huge allegorical statue of the Motherland on the top of the hill. The monument, designed by Yevgeny Vuchetich, has the full name The Motherland Calls! It consists of a concrete sculpture, 52 metres tall, and 85 metres from the feet to the tip of the 27-metre sword, dominating the skyline of the city of Stalingrad (later renamed Volgograd). The construction uses concrete, except for the stainless-steel blade of the sword, and is held on its plinth solely by its own weight. The statue is evocative of classical Greek representations of Nike, in particular the flowing drapery, similar to that of the Nike of Samothrace. ========================= Welcome to AboutWalk Channel! sourceDescription: Кабан (тат. Кабан күле) — система озёр, расположенных в городской черте Казани. Является самой крупной по площади озёрной системой в Татарстане. The Kaban Lakes (Tatar: Cyrillic Кабан күле, Latin Qaban küle, Arabic قابان كولئ; Russian: Кабан, lit. 'Boar') are a system of lakes in Kazan, Republic of Tatarstan, Russia that includes Nizhny (Blizhny) Kaban, Verkhny Kaban, and Sredny Kaban. With a combined area of 1.86 square kilometers (0.72 sq mi), they comprise the biggest lake in Tatarstan. Улица Баумана (тат. Бауман урамы, Bauman uramı) — пешеходная улица в историческом центре Казани, Вахитовском районе, ядро Казанского посада. Улица начинается около Казанского кремля от Площади Тысячелетия и продолжается на юго-восток до площади Тукая, где пересекается с улицей Пушкина. Baumana Street (Russian: улица Баумана; Tatar: Бауман урамы) is a pedestrian street in the heart of Kazan, the capital of the Tatarstan, Russia. It is named after Nikolay Bauman, a Russian revolutionary, and is located in the central part of the city. sourceDescription: Samara (Russian: Сама́ра, IPA: [sɐˈmarə]), known from 1935 to 1991 as Kuybyshev (Куйбышев; IPA: [ˈkujbɨʂɨf]), is the largest city and administrative centre of Samara Oblast. The city is located at the confluence of the Volga and the Samara rivers, with a population of over 1.1 million residents, up to 3 million residents in the urban agglomeration. The city covers an area of 541.382 square kilometers (209.029 sq mi), and is the eighth-largest city in Russia, the third-most populous city on the Volga, as well as the Volga Federal District. Formerly a closed city, Samara is now a large and important social, political, economic, industrial, and cultural centre in Russia and hosted the European Union—Russia Summit in May 2007. It has a continental climate characterised by hot summers and cold winters. The life of Samara's citizens has always been intrinsically linked to the Volga River, which has not only served as the main commercial thoroughfare of Russia throughout several centuries, but also has great visual appeal. Samara's riverfront is considered one of the favourite recreation places both for local citizens and tourists. After the Soviet novelist Vasily Aksyonov visited Samara, he remarked: "I am not sure where in the West one can find such a long and beautiful embankment. originalTitle: Walking tour in Curonian spit, Kaliningrad, Russia 4k
sourceDescription: Высота Эфа, Куршская коса Высота Эфа — вершина дюны Ореховой (Петш), одной из самых высоких дюн в Европе. Названа в честь немецкого ученого Вильгельма Франца Эфа, посвятившего свою жизнь восстановлению экологического равновесия на Куршской косе. Пешеходный экскурсионно-туристический маршрут. Вильгельм Франц Эфа (1826-1904) более 40 лет проработал дюнным инспектором Куршской косы и вошел в историю как победитель последствий «дюнной катастрофы». Ему принадлежит авторство проекта закрепления и облесения движущихся песчаных дюн. Curonian Spit National Park (Russian: Куршская коса) (Also: Kurshskaya Kosa) covers the Russian-owned southern 41 km of the 98 km long, curved Curonian Spit – a type of depositional sandbar. The spit separates the salt-water Baltic Sea (on the west) from the freshwater Curonian Lagoon to the east. The southern portion of the spit lies within Zelenogradsky District in Kaliningrad Oblast, Russia; the northern portion lies within southwestern Lithuania. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site shared by the two countries.

originalTitle: Walking in Kaliningrad Upper Pond, Russia 4K 60fps. | Верхний пруд, Калининград. (Part 2)
sourceDescription: Königsberg (UK: /ˈkɜːnɪɡzbɜːrɡ/, US: /ˈkeɪnɪɡzbɜːrɡ, ˈkʌn-/, German: [ˈkøːnɪçsˌbɛʁk] (About this soundlisten)) is the name for the historic Prussian city that is now Kaliningrad, Russia. Originally a Sambian or Old Prussian settlement, it then belonged to the State of the Teutonic Order, the Duchy of Prussia, the Kingdom of Prussia, the German Empire, the Weimar Republic, and Nazi Germany. After being largely destroyed in World War II by Allied bombing and the Red Army, it was annexed by the Soviet Union and its surviving inhabitants forcibly expelled. Thereafter, the city was renamed Kaliningrad. Few traces of the former Königsberg remain today. ( wikipedia ) The Upper Pond (Russian: Верхний пруд) is a large artificial pond in northern Kaliningrad, Russia. It was known as the Oberteich while part of Königsberg, Germany, until 1945. The pond is elevated 22 metres above the Pregel River and encompasses 41.1 hectares. Freshwater life living in the Upper Pond include perch, roach, carp, tench, pike, and eels. Located near the water is the Kaliningrad Amber Museum. Ве́рхний пруд (разг. Ве́рхнее о́зеро, до 1949 года — нем. Oberteich Обертайх) — пруд в городе Калининграде (Калининградская область, Россия). Берега Верхнего пруда являются зелёной рекреационной зоной.

originalTitle: Frombork - Poland, walking in Frombork 4K
sourceDescription: Morning walk around Frombork! Frombork is a town in northern Poland, situated on the Vistula Lagoon in Braniewo County, within Warmian-Masurian Voivodeship. It had a population of 2,415 as of 2016. The town was first mentioned in a 13th century document. In the early 16th century it was the residence of the astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus, who used it as a site for several of his observations. The town and its 700-year-old cathedral were badly damaged in World War II. After the war the cathedral was meticulously reconstructed and is again a popular tourist destination. Frombork is known as “The Jewel of Warmia” because of its many historical sites. The Museum of Copernicus in Frombork holds exhibitions related to the astronomer, as well as to astronomy in general, and includes a planetarium. sourceDescription: Kneiphof (Lithuanian: Knypava; Polish: Knipawa) was a quarter of central Königsberg, Germany. During the Middle Ages it was one of the three towns that composed the city of Königsberg, the others being Altstadt and Löbenicht. The town was located on a 10-hectare (25-acre) island of the same name in the Pregel River and included Königsberg Cathedral and the original campus of the University of Königsberg. Its territory is now part of the Moskovsky District of Kaliningrad, Russia. Кна́йпхоф (нем. Kneiphof, от прусского knypabe, «окружённое водой, рекой») — историческое название одной из островных городских частей Кёнигсберга и нынешнего Калининграда. Современное название — остров Иммануила Канта.

originalTitle: Walking in Kaliningrad Upper Pond, Russia 4K 60fps. | Верхний пруд, Калининград. (Part 1)
sourceDescription: The Upper Pond (Russian: Верхний пруд) is a large artificial pond in northern Kaliningrad, Russia. It was known as the Oberteich while part of Königsberg, Germany, until 1945. The pond is elevated 22 metres above the Pregel River and encompasses 41.1 hectares. Freshwater life living in the Upper Pond include perch, roach, carp, tench, pike, and eels. Located near the water is the Kaliningrad Amber Museum. Ве́рхний пруд (разг. Ве́рхнее о́зеро, до 1949 года — нем. Oberteich Обертайх) — пруд в городе Калининграде (Калининградская область, Россия). Берега Верхнего пруда являются зелёной рекреационной зоной. Königsberg (UK: /ˈkɜːnɪɡzbɜːrɡ/, US: /ˈkeɪnɪɡzbɜːrɡ, ˈkʌn-/,[1][2][3][4] German: [ˈkøːnɪçsˌbɛʁk] (About this soundlisten)) is the name for the historic Prussian city that is now Kaliningrad, Russia. Originally a Sambian or Old Prussian settlement, it then belonged to the State of the Teutonic Order, the Duchy of Prussia, the Kingdom of Prussia, the German Empire, the Weimar Republic, and Nazi Germany. After being largely destroyed in World War II by Allied bombing and the Red Army, it was annexed by the Soviet Union and its surviving inhabitants forcibly expelled. Thereafter, the city was renamed Kaliningrad. Few traces of the former Königsberg remain today. ( wikipedia )

sourceDescription: #куль_шариф #мечеть Каза́нский кремль (тат. Казан кирмәне, Qazan kirmäne) — древнейшая часть Казани, комплекс архитектурных, исторических и археологических памятников, раскрывающих многовековую историю города: археологические остатки первого (XII—XIII вв.), второго (XIV—XV вв.) и третьего городищ (XV—XVI вв.); белокаменный кремль, ряд храмов и зданий, имеющих большую историко-архитектурную и культурную ценность. Официальная резиденция Президента Республики Татарстан; объект Всемирного наследия ЮНЕСКО с 2000 года. The Kazan Kremlin (Russian: Казанский Кремль; Tatar: Казан кирмәне) is the chief historic citadel of Russia, situated in the city of Kazan. It was built at the behest of Ivan the Terrible on the ruins of the former castle of Kazan khans. It was declared a World Heritage Site in 2000. sourceDescription: Татарский государственный театр кукол «Экият» — крупнейший и один из старейших театров кукол в России. Находится в Казани на Петербургская улица в Вахитовском районе города. Название театра образовано от слова тат. әкият — «сказка». Построенное в виде сказочного замка-дворца здание театра является важной и популярной достопримечательностью города. Центр семьи «Казан» — главный дворец бракосочетаний (ЗАГС) в городе Казань и республике Татарстан. Одна из главных современных достопримечательностей города, обыгрывающих его название ввиду того, что построен в виде огромного котла-казана. На крыше расположена смотровая площадка с видом на Казанский кремль, Кремлёвскую набережную и округу. Открыт 5 июля 2013 года. #ЛетоВместе Puppet theatre ekiyat The new building of the theatre built in 2012 has already become one of the city's main attractions. With its stained-glass windows, white stone turrets and columns, it looks like a big fairytale castle. The theatre repertoire consists of over 50 performances, based on national tales of different countries around the world as well as modern works. The city sits on Tampa Bay as the largest city in the Tampa Bay area, and is the seat of Hillsborough County. Tampa functioned as a military center during the 19th century with the establishment of Fort Brooke. The cigar industry was also brought to the city by Vincente Martinez Ybor, after whom Ybor City is named. Tampa was formally reincorporated as a city in 1887, following the Civil War. Today, Tampa's economy is driven by tourism, health care, finance, insurance, technology, construction, and the maritime industry. The bay's port is the largest in the state, responsible for over $15 billion in economic impact. The city is part of the Tampa-St. Petersburg-Clearwater, Florida Metropolitan Statistical Area which is a four-county area composed of roughly 3.1 million residents, making it the second largest metropolitan statistical area (MSA) in the state and the fourth largest in the Southeastern United States, behind Washington, D.C., Miami, and Atlanta. The Greater Tampa Bay area has over 4 million residents and generally includes the Tampa and Sarasota metro areas. originalTitle: The Heart of Rostov in One Walk | City Streets in 4K
sourceDescription: I set off on a big walk through the center of Rostov-on-Don, filmed in 4K. My route runs from Voroshilovsky Avenue through Bolshaya Sadovaya Street, Budyonnovsky Avenue, Pushkinskaya Street, Semashko Lane, Moskovskaya Street and Soborniy Lane, ending at Maxim Gorky Park. In this video I show Rostov as it really is in everyday life: city streets, traffic, pedestrians, shops, old architecture and the everyday atmosphere of a southern city — no staging, no tourist filters. 📍 The walk starts on Voroshilovsky Avenue, which leads to the bridge over the Don. Over the years the avenue has gone through several name changes — it was once called Bolshoy Stolypinsky Avenue and then Karl Marx Avenue before being renamed after Voroshilov. 📍 On Bolshaya Sadovaya I walk along Rostov-on-Don's main street. It's hard to imagine that in the first half of the 19th century this area was considered an out-of-town fringe of the city — and that it was here that the first kerosene street lamps, running water, and electric trams later appeared. 📍 Budyonnovsky Avenue developed on the site of the old Taganrog Road, which led toward Taganrog and the Sea of Azov. In 1923 the avenue was named after Semyon Budyonny. 📍 Pushkinskaya Street is one of the greenest routes through the center of Rostov. After Chekhov Street it becomes a pedestrian zone, and at the intersection with Voroshilovsky Avenue there is a monument to Alexander Pushkin. 📍 I then pass through Semashko Lane, Moskovskaya Street and Soborniy Lane. Moskovskaya was once considered one of the city's main commercial streets and, unlike many streets in Rostov, has kept its historic name. Soborniy Lane leads to the Cathedral of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin and the Central Market, which locals still often call the Old Bazaar. 📍 The final stop on the route is Maxim Gorky Park. This is Rostov-on-Don's oldest city park, founded in 1813 on the site of private gardens. The park has two levels — the Upper and Lower Flower Gardens — and holds an important place at the heart of city life. ⏳ Timestamps: 00:00 – Intro 00:47 – Voroshilovsky Avenue 05:47 – Bolshaya Sadovaya Street 21:02 – Budyonnovsky Avenue 26:17 – Pushkinskaya Street 32:17 – Semashko Lane 42:27 – Moskovskaya Street 45:12 – Soborniy Lane 50:57 – Gorky Park Join me for this big 4K walk through Rostov-on-Don with Dima Walks 4K. sourceDescription: Welcome to Samara (Russia) Walking tour. Today is 27 of September 2021. Samara (Russian: Сама́ра, IPA: [sɐˈmarə]), known from 1935 to 1991 as Kuybyshev (Куйбышев; IPA: [ˈkujbɨʂɨf]), is the largest city and administrative centre of Samara Oblast. The city is located at the confluence of the Volga and the Samara rivers, with a population of over 1.14 million residents, up to 1,22 million residents in the urban agglomeration not including Novokubyshevsk actually not conurbated. The city covers an area of 541.382 square kilometers (209.029 sq mi), and is the eighth-largest city in Russia and tenth agglomeration, the third-most populous city on the Volga, as well as the Volga Federal District. Formerly a closed city, Samara is now a large and important social, political, economic, industrial, and cultural centre in Russia and hosted the European Union—Russia Summit in May 2007. It has a continental climate characterised by hot summers and cold winters. The life of Samara's citizens has always been intrinsically linked to the Volga River, which has not only served as the main commercial thoroughfare of Russia throughout several centuries, but also has great visual appeal. Samara's riverfront is considered one of the favourite recreation places both for local citizens and tourists. After the Soviet novelist Vasily Aksyonov visited Samara, he remarked: "I am not sure where in the West one can find such a long and beautiful embankment." 00:00 Crossing Kommunisticheskaya & Dachnaya streets 01:15 Iceberg Shopping Mall Shopping center of 2 floors. sourceDescription: This 4k HDR video was recorded in Voronezh, Russian on March 2021. Voronezh is a city in Central Russia straddling the Voronezh river and located 12 kilometres from where it flows into the Don river. It’s not far from Moscow, about 500 kilometres. Koltsov Aleksey Vasilievich was a Russian poet. His poems stylise peasant-life songs and idealise agricultural labour. Koltsov collected Russian folklore which strongly influenced his poetry. Bunin Ivan Alekseyevich was the first Russian writer awarded the Nobel Prize for Literature. He was noted for the strict artistry with which he carried on the classical Russian traditions in the writing of prose and poetry. sourceDescription: I’m taking a walk along Taganrogskaya Street in Rostov-on-Don. Filmed in 4K, this video captures everyday city life as it really is: the street, traffic, residential buildings, shops, daily routes and the ordinary rhythm of a major southern Russian city. Taganrogskaya Street is located in Rostov-on-Don’s Oktyabrsky District and is one of the city’s major thoroughfares. It stretches for approximately 4.9 kilometers and intersects with numerous other streets and lanes. Until 1958, Taganrogskaya Street was known as the North Caucasus Highway. It was later given its current name, referring to the city of Taganrog and the southern transport route. The history of the name is connected with the older Taganrog Road. A road leading toward Taganrog was already marked on a 1767 map of Rostov. Over time, this route became an important part of the city’s development and transport network. Today, Taganrogskaya is more than just a road — it is a major residential and urban corridor. Along the street, you’ll find apartment buildings, shops, public institutions, cultural venues and public transport stops. Bus routes running along the street connect Rostov’s residential neighborhoods with the Central Market and the railway station. Rostov-on-Don is one of the largest cities in southern Russia, located on the banks of the Don River. It is often called the “Gateway to the Caucasus” because of its important role in the transport and economic connections between the southern regions of the country. This is not a postcard view of Rostov. I’m simply walking along an ordinary street and showing its real atmosphere in high-quality 4K. originalTitle: Rostov in Golden Light | An Evening Walk Along Pushkinskaya Street in 4K
sourceDescription: I’m taking an evening walk along Pushkinskaya Street in Rostov-on-Don during golden hour. Filmed in 4K, this video captures the soft evening light, the warm tones of the façades, the greenery of the boulevard and the real life of the city — with no staging and no tourist filters. 🎥 Find more videos from Rostov-on-Don in the playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLTcleF0G4mHE Pushkinskaya is one of the best-known walking streets in Rostov-on-Don. It stretches for approximately 3.5 kilometers, running parallel to Bolshaya Sadovaya Street and connecting different parts of the city’s historic center. The street was once called Kuznetskaya, named after the blacksmiths who lived and worked here. In 1885, the city council renamed it Pushkinskaya in honor of Alexander Sergeyevich Pushkin. The poet himself did pass through Rostov in 1820 during his journey to the Caucasus with General Raevsky’s family. Later, his name became associated not only with the street but also with a monument in the city. The green character of modern-day Pushkinskaya began to take shape thanks to the initiative of tobacco manufacturer Yakov Kushnaryov and the workers at his factory. They planted trees and improved the street, gradually transforming what had once been the outskirts of the city into a leafy boulevard for walks. Pushkinskaya is home to a monument to Alexander Pushkin, unveiled in 1959. It was created by sculptor Gavriil Shults and architect Mikhail Minkus. It was the first literary monument in Rostov-on-Don. Part of the street has a distinctly pedestrian-friendly boulevard character. The section between Chekhov Street and Teatralny Prospekt is considered particularly pleasant for walking, as car traffic has little impact on the atmosphere. Historic mansions and tenement buildings from the late 19th and early 20th centuries have survived along Pushkinskaya. The street is also home to cultural institutions, including the Rostov Regional Museum of Fine Arts and the Don State Public Library, founded in 1886. During golden hour, Pushkinskaya becomes especially striking: sunlight filters through the tree canopies, falls across the façades and casts long shadows along the boulevard’s paths. In this video, I show the street as Rostov residents experience it every day — lively, green and authentic. Join me for a walk along Pushkinskaya Street with Dima Walks 4K. sourceDescription: Rostov Veliky is a town in Yaroslavl Oblast, Russia, one of the oldest in the country and a tourist center of the Golden Ring. It is located on the shores of Lake Nero, 202 kilometers (126 mi) northeast of Moscow. First mentioned in documents in the year 862 as an already important settlement, by the 10th century Rostov became the capital city of Vladimir-Suzdal, one of the most prominent principalities in Rus'. It was incorporated into the Grand Duchy of Moscow in 1474. After losing its independent status, Rostov was still an ecclesiastic center – from 988 it was the see of the Diocese of Yaroslavl, one of the first Russian bishoprics. In the 14th century, the bishops of Rostov became archbishops, and late in the 16th century, metropolitans. One of those metropolitans, Iona (Jonah) Sysoyevich (c. 1607–1690), commissioned the town's main landmark: the Rostov Kremlin. This is regarded by some as the finest outside that of Moscow.

originalTitle: Through Russia's Holiest Convent — 4K Walking Tour - Russian Orthodox Church, Diveyevo, Russia
sourceDescription: A slow, quiet walk through Diveyevo — one of the most sacred villages in Russia, home to the Holy Trinity Seraphim-Diveyevo Convent and the resting place of the relics of St. Seraphim of Sarov, one of the most venerated saints of the Russian Orthodox Church. The walk begins on Diveyevo's main street, past small market stalls selling clothes, souvenirs, and local sweets, and a quiet wooden guesthouse café. From there we enter the convent grounds — the most picturesque part of the walk — passing beneath a flower-covered arch toward the turquoise-and-gold Trinity Cathedral and the white Transfiguration Cathedral with its shining domes, across the open square, and along the holy springs and gardens inside the monastery walls. The walk ends outside the convent, following the calm, winding Vichkinza River, past a small wooden chapel, a weir, and an old footbridge. No talking, no narration — just the sounds of the walk and a quiet, soft instrumental soundtrack, so you can relax, unwind, and feel like you're actually there. 📍 Location: Diveyevo, Nizhny Novgorod Oblast, Russia 🎧 Best enjoyed with headphones 🕓 Filmed in spring (May 2026) 00:00 Intro — Quick preview 00:25 Diveyevo village street & market stalls 02:46 Entering the Holy Trinity Seraphim-Diveyevo Convent 03:00 Вelfry 03:24 Trinity Cathedral & the main square 03:59 The flower arch and Easter eggs 05:04 Holy spring & Transfiguration Cathedral 05:51 The main square 06:16 Monastery gardens 07:30 Holy spring of Venerable Alexandra 08:50 Leaving the convent — walking along the Vichkinza River 09:49 Weir 10:55 Footbridge If you enjoyed this walk, subscribe for more slow, immersive 4K walks through cities, villages, and quiet places around the world — and let me know in the comments where I should walk next. #Diveyevo #Russia #WalkingTour --- The Urban Walks — real walks around the world through the eyes of the traveler. Когда то это была деревня с одноимённым названием, но при расширении Нижнего Новгорда она была включена в состав города и на месте частных деревянных домов выросли панельные многоэтажки и хрущевки. Здесь довольно зелено, много скверов и аллей. Здесь хорошо развита инфраструктура - есть, кафе, рестораны, магазины, хорошо развита транспортная сеть. А ещё тут, в Щербинках, жил знаменитый академик, советский физик Андрей Дмитриевич Сахаров, когда находился в ссылке в городе Горьком. В квартире, где он жил, теперь располагается музей. Можете посетить! originalTitle: Samara city (Russia), random walking | 9:14 AM, May 10, 2024 | 1h 30m | 4k 60fps
Mayakovskiy, Vilonovskaya streets, Samara, Russia | Just Walk 4K | Маяковского, Вилоновская, Самара
sourceDescription: Welcome to Russia Walking tour. Today is 29 of September 2021. Samara is one of the best cities in Russia. Located on the Volga. Until 1991 it was called Kuibyshev, here is one of the largest squares in Europe, and a Zhiguli is nearby. Yes, even the fact that Zhigulevskoe beer was invented in Samara, I also did not know. As a result of the trip, I think that in vain - Samara is a very, very interesting city. In fact, Samara looks very, very attractive. This is not a collective farm with corresponding estates, but also not Petersburg, where the eye has nothing to cling to because of the abundance of attractions. Samara in the center is a prosperous provincial town of the late 19th century. Somewhere the history was preserved well, somewhere they did not give a damn about it, and in other places we will meet such houses surrounded by modern high-rise buildings. On the other hand, I don't remember any openly Soviet housing, such as the usual five-story buildings. Filmed: September 2021 Самара - один из лучших городов России. Находится на Волге. До 1991 года он назывался Куйбышев, здесь одна из самых больших площадей Европы, а рядом Жигули. Да даже то, что пиво «Жигулевское» изобрели в Самаре, я тоже не знал. По итогам поездки считаю, что зря - Самара очень и очень интересный город. На самом деле Самара выглядит очень и очень привлекательно. Это не колхоз с соответствующими имениями, но и не Петербург, где глазу не за что цепляться из-за обилия достопримечательностей. Самара в центре - процветающий провинциальный город конца 19 века. Где-то история сохранилась хорошо, где-то наплевать, а где-то мы встретим такие дома в окружении современных многоэтажек. С другой стороны, я не припомню ни одного откровенно советского жилья, типа обычных пятиэтажек. Снято: Сентябрь 2021

originalTitle: Kaliningrad - Russia - Walk @ 4K POV
sourceDescription: Amalienau was a suburban quarter of western Königsberg, Germany. Its territory is now part of the Tsentralny District of Kaliningrad, Russia. Амалиенау — район Кёнигсберга (нем. Amalienau), границы района: проспект Победы, ул. Лесопарковая, ул. Яналова и ул. Красная. Сейчас территория Амалиенау входит в Центральный административный район Калининграда. Амалиенау получил имя от дворянской усадьбы. В начале XX века находился ещё за городской чертой. Бурно развивался в 1900—1920 гг. в качестве района вилл богатых жителей Кёнигсберга в соответствии с концепцией «Город-сад».
